title: Algebraization of supported formal blowup towers with their centers
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian quasi-excellent scheme over $\mathbf Q$ [pqf-def-locnoeth, def-exc-excellent-ring], let $Z\subseteq X$ be a closed subscheme with coherent ideal $I$ [pqf-def-coherent], and put $\mathfrak X=\widehat X_Z$, with affine charts $\operatorname{Spf}(\varprojlim_n B/I^n)$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. A Noetherian scheme means one with a finite affine cover by spectra of Noetherian rings. A Noetherian adic formal scheme is a ringed space admitting a finite open cover by spaces of the form $\operatorname{Spf}B$, the space of open prime ideals of a Noetherian ring $B$ complete and separated for powers of a finitely generated ideal, with its completed structure sheaf. Such a formal scheme is reduced when its affine chart rings are reduced. Quasi-excellence means quasi-excellence of its affine chart rings [def-exc-excellent-ring]. Regularity of a formal scheme means regularity of the rings on its formal affine charts [def-weil-regular-scheme]. Its singular locus is defined on $\operatorname{Spf}B$ by the radical ideal of the nonregular locus of $\operatorname{Spec}B$. A formal blowup along a coherent ideal is obtained on each chart $\operatorname{Spf}B$ by taking the ordinary blowup of $\operatorname{Spec}B$ in the center ideal and then completing along the extended original ideal of definition [def-nagata-global-blowup, pqf-def-coherent]. A tower retains its ordered center ideals, including centers whose blowups happen to be isomorphisms. A center at a level over $X$ is $Z$-supported if its ideal contains a power of the extended ideal $I$; use the same definition for formal centers. Completion gives a bijection, up to unique isomorphism preserving all the ordered ideals and the base, between finite $Z$-supported ordinary blowup towers over $X$ with coherent ideals and finite supported formal blowup towers over $\mathfrak X$ with coherent open ideals. At corresponding stages the ordinary center and formal center are canonically the same closed scheme, so nonemptiness and regularity of the centers agree. Corresponding ordinary levels complete to the specified formal levels. If $X_{\mathrm{sing}}\subseteq |Z|$, then a formal tower with regular last level and centers lying over $\mathfrak X_{\mathrm{sing}}$ corresponds to an ordinary tower with regular last level and centers lying over $X_{\mathrm{sing}}$. If also $X$ is reduced [def-pc-reduced-scheme], these centers are nowhere dense in their respective ordinary levels. Here $X_{\mathrm{sing}}$ is the reduced closed subscheme of nonregular points, and $\mathfrak X_{\mathrm{sing}}$ is its completion. Empty stages and the length-zero tower are included in the correspondence.

source.place: Lemma 2.4.3(i)--(ii), printed pp.15--16, with §§2.2.1--2.2.2,2.3.1,2.4.6--2.4.11; nowhere density for reduced X is the elementary generic-point consequence of singular support. No Stacks tag states this centered formal-tower correspondence. Read online 2026-10-24; archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Work first on an arbitrary Noetherian ordinary level $Y$, with $K=I\mathcal O_Y$, and an affine $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\subset Y$. Write $\widehat A=\varprojlim A/K(U)^n$. For a supported formal center ideal $H\subset\widehat A$, choose $N\ge1$ with $K(U)^N\widehat A\subset H$. The canonical quotient theorem [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-power] identifies $\widehat A/K(U)^N\widehat A$ with $A/K(U)^N$. Define $J\subset A$ as the inverse image of $H/K(U)^N\widehat A$ under $A\to A/K(U)^N$. Then $K(U)^N\subset J$, $J\widehat A=H$, and $A/J\cong\widehat A/H$: all three assertions follow by taking inverse images under the same surjective quotient map. Conversely, for $J\supset K(U)^N$, contraction of $J\widehat A$ is $J$, by that quotient identification. Thus these operations are inverse on supported ideals, independently of a larger choice of $N$. No faithful flatness of $A\to\widehat A$ away from $V(K(U))$ is asserted.

source.place: Tag 05GG, lemma-hathat-finitely-generated; ideal preimages in its canonical finite quotients

proof.text: The local inverse ideals glue. On a principal open $D(f)\subset U$, both ordinary and completed quotients modulo $K^N$ are $(A/K(U)^N)_f$. Therefore the inverse image ideal on $D(f)$ is $J_f$; this is the elementary localization of the quotient map $A\to A/J$. On arbitrary intersections use principal affine refinements, without assuming the intersections affine. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-affine-ideals-closed-subscheme] to obtain a global quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal J$ and its closed subscheme. It is coherent: on any affine neighbourhood its ideal is a finite module over a Noetherian ring, and the kernel of a map from a finite free module into that ideal is finite for the same reason; restriction to affine neighbourhoods gives exactly the coherence condition [pqf-def-coherent]. A finite affine cover permits a common exponent $N$ (take the maximum). Conversely completion of $\mathcal J$ recovers the original formal ideal on each chart. The centers are canonically the same scheme, glued from $\operatorname{Spec}(A/J)=\operatorname{Spec}(\widehat A/H)$, and this identification is over the closed thickening defined by $K^N$.

source.place: Tag 01XZ, lemma-coherent-Noetherian (affine finite-kernel argument written out); Temkin Lemma 2.4.3(i), first sentence of the proof

proof.text: Every resulting ordinary blowup level is again Noetherian. Its center is a coherent ideal, hence of finite type by [pqf-def-coherent]. By [thm-nagata-global-blowup-proper] its blowup morphism is proper, hence of finite type by [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] gives a Noetherian source. These implications apply to nonreduced schemes and also to the zero and unit ideals. Thus Step 1 and Step 2 remain applicable after each blowup, without adding a reducedness hypothesis.

Completion commutes with the ordinary blowup, with the extended ideal retained. On $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$, $A\to\widehat A$ is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-completion-flat]. Apply [thm-nagata-blowup-flat-base-change] with the comparison specified by [def-nagata-blowup-flat-base-change-map]: $\operatorname{Bl}_{J\widehat A}(\operatorname{Spec}\widehat A)\cong\operatorname{Spec}\widehat A\times_U\operatorname{Bl}_J(U)$. For any affine $\operatorname{Spec}C$ in the latter ordinary blowup, the base-changed affine ring is $C\otimes_A\widehat A$. Its quotient by $K^n$ is canonically $C\otimes_A(A/K(U)^n)=C/K^nC$, by [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-power]. The map sends $c\otimes\widehat a$ to $c\overline{\widehat a}$ and respects every transition in $n$. Taking the inverse limit, as defined by [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], identifies the two completed chart rings. These maps respect restrictions because their quotient formulas do, so they glue. By definition, a formal blowup on an affine chart is the completion of the ordinary blowup of its complete chart ring; thus this is precisely the required comparison of formal levels, not base change along a nonflat finite quotient. The completed chart rings are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-noetherian].

source.place: Tag 0805, lemma-flat-base-change-blowing-up; algebra.tex Tags 00MB and 05GG; Temkin §2.4.6

proof.text: Induct on the given finite length $r$. For $r=0$, the ordinary level is the specified $X$ and its completion is the specified $\mathfrak X$. Given the first $i$ ordinary blowups with their specified formal comparisons, use Step 2 on $Y=X_i$ to recover the unique supported ideal $J_i$ of the next formal center. Put $X_{i+1}=\operatorname{Bl}_{J_i}(X_i)$; Step 3 permits the next induction and Step 4 supplies the specified comparison of its completion with the next formal level. Conversely, complete each level and each ordered ideal of an ordinary tower. Steps 1--2 recover each original ideal; Step 4 recovers each level. These two operations are inverse on the centered towers, preserving all indices and all structure maps. In particular, no stage is removed merely because its morphism is an isomorphism.

source.place: Lemma 2.4.3(i), proof, printed pp.15--16; explicit finite induction

proof.text: The isomorphisms of centered towers are unique. On an ordinary blowup the extended center ideal is invertible by [thm-nagata-blowup-principalizes-center]. The finite chart cover of [prop-nagata-affine-blowup-chart-cover] has rings $C=A[J/a]\subset A_a$ [def-nagata-blowup-chart-ring]. The $a$-chart is intrinsically the locus where $a$ generates the extended ideal: on a $b$-chart it is the open where $a/b$ is a unit. Thus a base automorphism preserves it. On the $a$-chart, multiplication by $a$ is injective, and $a(j/a)=j$ forces the automorphism to fix every $j/a$, hence $C$. For the formal blowup repeat this calculation on completed charts: $C\to\widehat C$ is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-completion-flat], so multiplication by $a$ remains injective. The rings $C$ are Noetherian by Step 3. An automorphism over the formal base fixes all the ratios, hence the dense image of $C$, and is the identity on $\widehat C$ by continuity and separatedness of the adic topology. Induction over the tower proves uniqueness; the same ratio calculation makes the comparisons of Step 4 the unique ones over the preceding level.

source.place: Tags 01OF (section-blowing-up), 02OS (lemma-blowing-up-gives-effective-Cartier-divisor); affine ratio proof of rigidity written out; algebra.tex Tag 00MB for completed charts

proof.text: The center identification in Step 2 is an isomorphism of actual closed schemes, so it preserves nonemptiness and regularity, not only their underlying supports. Its structural map is over the same thickening of $X$. Hence a formal center lying over the completion of $X_{\mathrm{sing}}$ gives an ordinary center whose image lies in $X_{\mathrm{sing}}$: its points lie over $Z$, and on $Z$ the completed singular locus has precisely the points of $X_{\mathrm{sing}}\cap Z$. Here the stipulated base singular subscheme is $\mathfrak X_{\mathrm{sing}}=\widehat{(X_{\mathrm{sing}})}_Z$. Each ordinary center is supported on the inverse image of $Z$, so its ideal is the unit ideal on the inverse image of $X\setminus Z$. Apply [thm-nagata-global-blowup-complement] and restrict its isomorphism to this open at each stage. Thus every ordinary level is canonically isomorphic to $X\setminus Z$ away from that inverse image.

source.place: Lemma 2.4.3(ii); §2.4.9, singular locus under completion; preservation of the center as a finite-thickening scheme from Steps 1--2

proof.text: Suppose $X_{\mathrm{sing}}\subset |Z|$ and the last formal level is regular. Put $Y=X_r$. Step 7 identifies $Y$ away from the inverse image of $Z$ with the regular scheme $X\setminus Z$. At a point $y\in Y$ over $Z$, take an affine neighbourhood $\operatorname{Spec}A\subset Y$, its ideal $K=I\mathcal O_Y(\operatorname{Spec}A)$, and the prime $\mathfrak p$ of $y$. Since $K\subset\mathfrak p$, the quotient isomorphism $\widehat A/K\widehat A\cong A/K$ of [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-power] gives a prime $\mathfrak q\subset\widehat A$ contracting to $\mathfrak p$. The local map $A_{\mathfrak p}\to\widehat A_{\mathfrak q}$ is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-completion-flat]. Both local rings are Noetherian, using Step 3 and [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-noetherian]. The target is regular because $\operatorname{Spf}\widehat A$ is an affine chart of the specified regular last formal level. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-under-regular] to this local map. It gives regularity at $y$. This covers every point of $Y$, so $Y$ is regular. No assertion that adic completion is faithfully flat on the whole affine spectrum is used.

source.place: Tags 05GG, 00MB, 0316, 00OF (lemma-flat-under-regular); local proof of the regular-terminal clause of Temkin Lemma 2.4.3(ii)

proof.text: Finally assume $X$ reduced and the centers lie over $X_{\mathrm{sing}}$. A component generic point of a reduced Noetherian scheme has a reduced zero-dimensional Noetherian local ring, hence a field (its unique prime is its nilradical, which is zero); so every component generic point of $X$ is regular. Inductive claim for $i\le r$: $X_i$ is reduced and Noetherian, and each component generic point of $X_i$ maps to a component generic point of $X$. It holds for $i=0$. Given it for $i$, the center $V(J_i)$ has image in $X_{\mathrm{sing}}$, so it contains no component generic point of $X_i$. A nonempty open subset of $X_i$ meets some irreducible component in a nonempty open of it, hence contains its generic point; so the center is nowhere dense. By [lem-per-reduced-noetherian-blowup-geometry], $X_{i+1}=\operatorname{Bl}_{J_i}(X_i)$ is reduced and Noetherian. Let $\eta$ be a component generic point of $X_{i+1}$; its local ring is a field. By [thm-nagata-blowup-principalizes-center], near $\eta$ the ideal $J_i\mathcal O_{X_{i+1}}$ is generated by a nonzerodivisor $g$ of an affine chart ring; localization is exact, so $g$ is a nonzerodivisor, hence a unit, in the field at $\eta$. Thus $\eta$ lies in $b^{-1}(U)$, $U=X_i\setminus V(J_i)$, an open subscheme isomorphic to $U$ by [thm-nagata-global-blowup-complement]. So $\eta$ is a component generic point of the open $U$, hence of $X_i$ (the closure in $X_i$ of an irreducible component of $U$ is an irreducible component of $X_i$), and maps to one of $X$ by the inductive claim. Consequently every center is nowhere dense in its ordinary level; no normalization is used.

source.place: Tags 0808, lemma-blow-up-reduced-scheme, and 0BFM, lemma-blow-up-and-irreducible-components (its proof: the exceptional divisor is effective Cartier and the complement maps isomorphically); generic-point induction for the reduced clause

proof.text: All constructions include the edge cases. If $Z=\varnothing$, then $I=\mathcal O_X$ and the supported ordinary ideals are all unit ideals; the formal base is empty and it likewise has one ideal at each retained index. If $Z=X$ with $I=0$, completion is the original discrete scheme and the correspondence is the identity. More generally a nilpotent ideal of definition causes no change in the finite-quotient argument. A unit center is empty and gives an identity blowup, but remains a recorded stage. A zero center is allowed when supported (then a power of the ideal of definition is zero); its blowup is empty, and subsequent empty levels and their ideals remain in order. The induction handles the empty base and the length-zero tower without selecting a center.
